what_its_for: Canagliflozin is used to help lower blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It works by causing your kidneys to remove extra sugar from your body through your urine. It may also help protect your kidneys and reduce the risk of heart problems in people who have both type 2 diabetes and heart or kidney disease.
how_to_take: Take canagliflozin by mouth, with or without food. It is best taken before your first meal of the day. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist tells you it is okay. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 100 mg once daily taken before your first meal. Your doctor may increase your dose to 300 mg once daily if your blood sugar is not well controlled and your kidneys are working well enough. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different based on your kidney function and other health conditions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store canagliflozin at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, as this can increase your risk of a rare but serious condition called ketoacidosis (a dangerous buildup of acids in the blood). Avoid becoming dehydrated — drink enough water each day, especially in hot weather or during exercise. Tell your doctor before having surgery, as you may need to stop this medicine temporarily. Avoid skipping meals, as this can cause your blood sugar to drop too low, especially if you take other diabetes medicines. Avoid foot injuries — check your feet daily for cuts, sores, or blisters, as canagliflozin may increase the risk of foot problems including rare cases of toe or foot amputation.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: signs of a serious genital infection such as pain, redness, swelling, or a bad smell around your genitals or buttocks (this could be a rare but life-threatening infection called Fournier's gangrene); signs of a urinary tract infection such as burning when you urinate, frequent urination, or blood in your urine; signs of ketoacidosis such as nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, tiredness, or trouble breathing; signs of low blood pressure such as dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting; signs of low blood sugar such as shakiness, sweating, rapid heartbeat, or confusion; pain or tenderness in your feet or toes; decreased urination or signs of kidney problems; or a broken bone after a minor injury.
when_it_works: Canagliflozin starts working within the first few days to lower blood sugar levels. However, it may take several weeks to see the full benefit on your blood sugar control. Your doctor will check your blood sugar and kidney function regularly to see how well the medicine is working for you.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and over): You may have a higher risk of side effects such as dizziness and dehydration. Your doctor will monitor you closely and may start you on a lower dose. Kidney disease: This medicine may not work as well or may not be safe if your kidneys are not functioning well. Your doctor will check your kidney function before and during treatment. Pregnancy: Canagliflozin should NOT be used during the second or third trimester of pregnancy as it may harm the unborn baby. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if canagliflozin passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medicine. Children: Canagliflozin is not approved for use in children under 18 years of age.
